penicillin.label: Penicillin class
penicillin.note: A documented penicillin allergy is a direct contraindication to other penicillins. Cross-reactivity with cephalosporins exists but is lower than once believed; the decision belongs to the prescriber.

cephalosporin.label: Cephalosporin class
cephalosporin.note: Partial cross-reactivity with penicillins, mainly where side chains are similar.

sulfonamide.label: Sulfonamide antibiotics
sulfonamide.note: Sulfonamide antibiotic allergy does not reliably predict reactions to non-antibiotic sulfonamides such as furosemide or hydrochlorothiazide, but it should still be discussed with the prescriber.

nsaid.label: NSAIDs and aspirin
nsaid.note: People who react to one NSAID often react to others, because the reaction is usually related to COX-1 inhibition rather than to a single molecule.

macrolide.label: Macrolide antibiotics
macrolide.note: Reactions to one macrolide may extend to others in the class.

fluoroquinolone.label: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics
fluoroquinolone.note: Class-wide caution after a reaction to any fluoroquinolone.

tetracycline.label: Tetracycline antibiotics
tetracycline.note: Class-wide caution after a reaction to any tetracycline.

opioid.label: Opioid analgesics
opioid.note: Many reported opioid 'allergies' are predictable side effects (nausea, itching) rather than true allergy, but true allergy does occur. The distinction matters and should be made by a clinician.

statin.label: Statins
statin.note: Muscle-related intolerance to one statin does not always extend to others; switching is a prescriber decision.

ssri.label: SSRI antidepressants
ssri.note: True allergy is uncommon; previous reactions should still be recorded.

benzodiazepine.label: Benzodiazepines
benzodiazepine.note: Class-wide caution after a documented reaction.

azole.label: Azole antifungals
azole.note: Class-wide caution after a documented reaction.
